script.base: NYG at CHI, Week 10, Sunday 1:00 ET, outdoors. Closing line in the pack is CHI -4.5 with a 45.5 total, so the book has Chicago leading a competitive game, not a blowout: implied team totals CHI 25.0 and NYG 20.5. Base script is a one-score Bears lead into the fourth quarter. Chicago has already been run-heavy in weeks 7-9 (Kyle Monangai 46 carries for 281 yards, D'Andre Swift 30 for 169, Caleb Williams 10 for 77, Brittain Brown 5 for 37), and a favorite at -4.5 should keep feeding the lead back late. New York, the 4.5-point dog with center John Michael Schmitz out, is the side that has to throw if it trails: Wan'Dale Robinson drew 27 targets for 189 yards and 230 air yards in that same three-game window, with Theo Johnson 17/113/114 and Darius Slayton 12/88/159 behind him. Pace stays moderate on 45.5, not a London-style shootout and not a 38-point slog.
script.flip1: Chicago jumps out early and clocks it. Monangai carries stack, Williams and the Bears wideouts (Rome Odunze, DJ Moore, Olamide Zaccheaus) stall the way a clock-kill favorite's passing stats stall, and the Giants abandon the run so Cam Skattebo (only 19 carries / 72 yards in the weeks 7-9 window) and Tyrone Tracy Jr. (24/103) lose the rushing line while Jaxson Dart's attempts rise. Dart has been a runner himself (18 carries / 85 yards in that window), but NYG EPA per dropback is -0.06 against the blitz versus +0.05 when not blitzed, and Chicago blitzes 30 percent, so extra attempts do not guarantee yards.
script.flip2: The Giants hang around or lead. Both quarterbacks throw, Robinson plus Moore/Loveland clear, and Chicago's run share drops so Monangai's carry total comes in closer to a split with Swift than to 15 carries. The other flip is an unsaved outdoor weather turn (wind 15+ or rain) that drags 45.5 under and cuts deep air yards (Odunze had 263 air yards on 19 targets in the window; Slayton 159 air on only 12 targets).

injury_fallout: Morning-of report only. Final inactives about 90 minutes before the 13:00 ET kick are not in the pack, so any leg a late scratch touches has to be re-checked and is not locked. He is still in the weeks 7-9 carry log (30/169) but Monangai already out-carried him 46 to 30, so a limited or inactive Swift pushes an even larger share to Monangai rather than to Brittain Brown (5 carries / 37 yards). Durham Smythe is Questionable (calf); Colston Loveland already has the TE receiving role (16 targets / 180 yards / 129 air) against Cole Kmet (3/26/43), so Smythe sitting does not create a new starter, it protects Loveland's share. Jahdae Walker is Out (concussion), a depth receiver, not a target thief from Moore or Odunze. Chicago defense: T.J. Edwards is Out (hand), the linebacker absence that helps Giants tight ends, backs and the middle (Chicago already allows 9.75 YPA on 61 middle attempts). Josh Blackwell is Out (concussion), a corner, which helps slot/perimeter options if he was playing. Dominique Robinson is Out (ankle), a pass-rush loss, which slightly helps Dart's time to throw. Giants offense: John Michael Schmitz is Out (shin) and Jermaine Eluemunor is Questionable (pectoral). That is center plus a tackle: pressure rate up, rushing efficiency down, more quick throws. That hurts Skattebo and Tracy rushing overs and helps short targets (Johnson, Bellinger 5 targets but 109 yards, Skattebo and Tracy as receivers). Beaux Collins is Out (neck), depth only; he is not why Nabers is missing from the weeks 7-9 target log. Graham Gano is Out (neck), a kicking note only, irrelevant to these yardage props. Giants defense: Paulson Adebo is Out (knee), the named corner absence for Moore and Odunze. Jevon Holland is Questionable (knee); if he sits, deep shots (Odunze 263 air yards) get easier, but he is not ruled out. Darius Muasau is Out (ankle) and Victor Dimukeje is Doubtful (shoulder): two linebackers down in front of a run defense that already allows 5.79 YPC and 43 runs of 10+ in 9 games. That is the Monangai and Loveland fallout. Chauncey Golston is Out (neck), another pass-rush loss, which fits Chicago's EPA/db of +0.23 when blitzed versus +0.14 when not. Malik Nabers is not on this report. He also has zero targets in the weeks 7-9 Giants log and the prop median is built on only 4 games (last4 receiving yards 71, 167, 13, 20). Role today is unknown, so he is not a leg. Sources: nflverse injury report and weeks 7-9 logs in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man-versus-zone charting was saved for NYG at CHI, so shell is inferred from location splits only. Chicago defense, 8 games: YPA left 8.15 on 92 attempts, middle 9.75 on 61, right 7.37 on 87. The Bears bleed the middle, then the left, not a locked-down outside shell. New York defense, 9 games: YPA left 6.69 on 116 attempts, middle 8.59 on 59, right 6.70 on 143. The Giants' perimeter is ordinary; the middle is the hole. Against a zone-lean or a linebacker-light front, the matchup for Chicago is the hook, middle and backs, which is Loveland and the running backs, not automatically the outside corner.
matchup.pressure: Both teams blitz 30 percent. Giants EPA per dropback is -0.06 versus the blitz and +0.05 with no blitz, so Chicago pressure kills Dart's deep yards (Robinson 230 air yards and Slayton 159 air yards in three games are the vulnerable chunk) and pushes checkdowns to Johnson, Bellinger, Skattebo and Tracy. Chicago EPA per dropback is +0.23 versus the blitz and +0.14 with no blitz, so Williams has been better, not worse, when New York brings pressure. Golston is out and Dimukeje is doubtful, which further lowers the chance New York's pressure actually gets home. Schmitz out and Eluemunor questionable are the Giants' own protection problem, independent of the blitz rate.
matchup.bleeds: New York run defense is the loudest bleed on the card: 5.79 yards per carry and 43 runs of 10-plus in 9 games, now with Muasau out and Dimukeje doubtful. Chicago run defense is also soft (5.18 YPC, 29 runs of 10-plus in 8 games) and Edwards is out, but the Giants do not have a single back with Monangai's carry share to attack it. Chicago pass defense: 31 completions or plays of 20-plus for 257 yards, middle 9.75 YPA. New York pass defense: 25 plays of 20-plus for 339 yards, so the explosives that do happen go for more, and Adebo is already out with Holland questionable.
matchup.overlap: The core overlap is Chicago's current primary run option, Kyle Monangai (46 carries, 281 yards, 6.1 yards per carry in weeks 7-9), running at the exact spot the Giants give up (5.79 YPC, linebackers out or doubtful). The second overlap is Colston Loveland (16 targets, 180 yards, 129 air yards in that window) into the Giants' middle (8.59 YPA on 59 attempts) with those same linebackers missing, and Smythe questionable so the TE job is not split. DJ Moore (18 targets, 188 yards, 183 air) is the passed alternate: Adebo out helps him, but New York's outside YPA (6.69 left, 6.70 right) is not the bleed, the middle is. Wan'Dale Robinson (27 targets, 189 yards) overlaps Chicago's middle and Edwards' absence, but Schmitz/Eluemunor plus a negative EPA versus a 30 percent blitz is the wrong setup for a 48.5 receiving-yard over after games of 48 and 46.

form: Window totals, not per-game averages: they reconcile to the newest games on the last4 lists. Treat last4 as oldest to newest. Kyle Monangai rush last4 19, 81, 24, 176 and the weeks 7-9 total is 281, which is 81+24+176. The role change is the story; the 19-yard game is the old role. Even the quiet game inside the new role (24) cleared a 21.5 rush line. Receiving in that window was 8 targets for 35 yards, so the edge is rushing, not the 9.5 receiving line. D'Andre Swift rush last4 38, 108, 124, 45. The 169-yard weeks 7-9 total equals 124+45 only, so he may have missed one week in the window, and the latest game is 45 with a groin tag. Do not over 53.5. Colston Loveland receiving last4 11, 24, 38, 118; weeks 7-9 total 180 equals 24+38+118. Trend is up. Two of the last four are under 24.5 (11 and 24), so this is a lean, not a smash, once the 118 is treated as one explosive. DJ Moore last4 42, 43, 73, 72; weeks 7-9 188 equals 43+73+72. Steadier than Loveland, just under the line once (43 vs 44.5), then 73 and 72. Rome Odunze last4 32, 31, 114, 0; weeks 7-9 145 equals 31+114+0. Most recent zero with 263 air yards in the window is a pass, not an over 49.5, even with Adebo out. Olamide Zaccheaus last4 24, 9, 33, 58; window 100 yards on 18 targets versus a 28.5 line, a coin flip. Wan'Dale Robinson last4 84, 95, 48, 46; window 189 equals 95+48+46. Nine targets a game, but the last two games are 48 and 46 against a 48.5 line, trending the wrong way for an over. Theo Johnson last4 27, 66, 20, 27; window 113 equals 66+20+27. One spike, then 20 and 27 against 27.5. Cam Skattebo rush last4 59, 98, 60, 12, but the weeks 7-9 rush line is only 19 carries for 72 yards, which matches 60+12 rather than 98+60+12, so the recent window is a reduced share behind Tracy (24/103) and Dart (18/85). That is an under-59.5 usage read fighting a bad Chicago run defense and Edwards being out, so it is not a leg. Tyrone Tracy Jr. rush last4 6, 46, 39, 18; window 24 carries for 103 yards (about 34 a game) versus a 24.5 line, with Schmitz out. Not clean. Malik Nabers is absent from the weeks 7-9 target list entirely. Sources: pack weeks 7-9 logs and the last4 lines on the available props.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and the NYG@CHI card lost. Monangai's 176 was the outlier, Swift played through the groin and took the carries the way he did in the 108- and 124-yard games, and the Giants' backup linebackers fit the run well enough that Monangai's day looked like the 19-yard sample rather than 81 or 176. Or Chicago fell behind, Dart and Robinson made it a pass script, and the lead-back carry assumption died. Loveland's 118 was one play. With Adebo out, Williams fed Moore (73 and 72 in the last two) and Odunze instead of the tight end, and a clock-killing 25-point script left Loveland at 11 or 24. The process error would be treating a season-median stand-in (21.5 and 24.5) as a close. Unsaved wind at an outdoor 1:00 ET kick, or a late active designation for Swift, Holland or Smythe, is the checkpoint that would have killed the read and was not available in this pack.
slip_story: One NYG@CHI Chicago-control story only: favorite leads on a 25.0 implied total, lead back Kyle Monangai rush yards over, and tight end Colston Loveland receiving yards over against the same depleted Giants linebacker group. Those two can win together because Loveland's 16 targets already happened in the window where Monangai had 46 carries. Do not mix in a game under, a Giants passing over (Robinson or Johnson), a Skattebo or Tracy rushing over, or any touchdown. Do not add Moore as a third leg. No bet is placed; prices were never saved.
